summary: Observed 2026-10-31 for FS.GG.Execution.Contracts and Processes 0.3.1: packages.lock.json contentHash equals the base64 SHA-512 of the candidate nupkg as packed, not of the nupkg nuget.org serves. nuget.org adds a repository signature (.signature.p7s, every other member byte-identical; served sha256 differs from the candidate), and the restored package's .nupkg.sha512 differs from the lock contentHash. So locks regenerated against the hosted candidate (SDK 10.0.401, candidate feed) were identical, for the Execution rows, to locks regenerated later from nuget.org alone (SDK 10.0.403): a lock made from a candidate feed stays valid after publication. Consequences: do not compare a lock contentHash with the sha256 or .nupkg.sha512 of a served signed package, and compare publication payloads member by member (the workflow's cache-identity and payload-match checks normalize this). This is an observation for these two packages and these SDKs, not a NuGet specification.
title: NuGet lock contentHash covers the unsigned package content, not the signed file
